explainer: Cortland (New York, USA) sorts its lines into numbered price tiers plus named series. The 333 series ($49.95) is the entry tier, and the 444 Classic series ($69.95) holds the heritage lines. The 444 Classic lines are 444 Peach (the 50-year all-rounder, 32 ft head), 444 Sylk (a softer 37 ft head line aimed at bamboo and glass rods) and 444 SL (a 41 ft head, 105 ft distance line), each with double-taper versions.

The wider 444 series ($69.95) adds Modern Trout (half size heavy, 48 ft head, for fast rods), Spring Creek, Big Shot, Hover, clear and camo intermediates, full sinkers and sink tips. The $99.95 premium series are split by job. Trout covers Finesse Trout II, Ultralight II, Indicator II, Trout Boss, Headwater and Trout Double Taper, and Streamer covers 26-40 ft heads with floating, intermediate and Type 3/6 tips.

Specialty covers bass, pike/musky, the grain-rated Compact heads, Ghost Tip clear tips and Salmon Steelhead. Tropic Plus covers hard-coated mono-core tropical lines, and Liquid Crystal is the premium clear and PE-coated tropical line. Cold Salt uses supple braided-core lines for cold-water stripers and redfish, and 50+ is big-game. Kelly Galloup signature streamer lines cost $129.95, Euro Nymph lines $59.95, and Fairplay is the $29.95 budget brand.

The Competition series (Fo-Tech 130 ft distance lines and Seek sinkers) now sells only in the clearance 'warehouse', so it is listed as discontinued. Cortland labels heaviness explicitly, for example 'true line size', 'half line size heavy' (Modern Trout, Guide, Tropic Redfish) and 'full line size heavy' (Trout Boss, Big Shot, Streamer, Bass, Indicator II). Buyers should match the heaviness label to rod speed (heavy for fast modern rods, true-to-size or Sylk for slower rods), then pick a series by water type.
